body:
**Adrian ([@thiefmaster](https://github.com/thiefmaster)) wrote:**

Adding this solves the problem, but no idea if it's the proper way:

```python
    def _set_parent(self, column):
        TypeDecorator._set_parent(self, column)
        SchemaType._set_parent(self, column)

    def _set_parent_with_dispatch(self, parent):
        TypeDecorator._set_parent_with_dispatch(self, parent)
        SchemaType._set_parent_with_dispatch(self, parent)
```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Well, _set_table() is a private method anyway.   I'm all for supporting your use case but I think you'd want to use normal event hooks here.

**Adrian ([@thiefmaster](https://github.com/thiefmaster)) wrote:**

How would I do this with event hooks on the type level (i.e. without having to add extra code for each model using the type)?

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

so *thats* the bug, that before_parent_attach() seems to not be working when TypeDecorator is involved.

```
from sqlalchemy import *
from sqlalchemy.types import SchemaType
from sqlalchemy import event


class MyType(SchemaType, TypeDecorator):
    impl = String
    pass


@event.listens_for(MyType, "before_parent_attach")
def go(target, parent):
    print "yes"

Column('q', MyType())
```

**Changes by Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)):**

* changed **title** from "_set_table not called in 1.1 on custom type based " to "TypeDecorator / SchemaType combination not firing "

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

which is ....because this style of inheritance has never been tested or done before.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

yep so this is #2919 in ed535649d423020c816e66869016992df25e456e , which ensured that the vastly more typical approach of TypeDecorator *around* the SchemaType worked, and at the same time never thought the TypeDecorator *itself* would be the SchemaType.

**Adrian ([@thiefmaster](https://github.com/thiefmaster)) wrote:**

Thanks!

Small suggestion for the docs: Mention when to use before/after parent attach (what's the reason in your example to use before on the type level but then after on the column level)?

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

well you're doing "e.table is table" so that event needs to be "after".  The outer event is "before" because I just tend to use that event first, it's before things have been set up so tends to be more useful.  might work either way here.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Ensure TypeDecorator delegates _set_parent_with_dispatch

Ensure TypeDecorator delegates _set_parent_with_dispatch as well as
_set_parent to itself as well as its impl, as the TypeDecorator
class itself may have an active SchemaType implementation as well.

Fixed regression which occurred as a side effect of :ticket:`2919`,
which in the less typical case of a user-defined
:class:`.TypeDecorator` that was also itself an instance of
:class:`.SchemaType` (rather than the implementation being such)
would cause the column attachment events to be skipped for the
type itself.

Change-Id: I0afb498fd91ab7d948e4439e7323a89eafcce0bc
Fixes: #3832


→ 30bd28fca209

**Changes by Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)):**

* changed **status** to closed

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

same issue with ARRAY.  See #4141

this is the same issue as #3832


```

my_type = ARRAY(String)


@event.listens_for(my_type, "before_parent_attach")
```

issue.title: Duplicate CheckConstraint for custom type

labels.name: schema
labels.description: things related to the DDL related objects like Table, Column, CreateIndex, etc.

labels.name: datatypes
labels.description: things to do with database types, like VARCHAR and others

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
I've created a custom column type, which converts "Y" and "N" from within the database to `True` and `False` in the python context and vice versa. I choose to implement it as an enum type.

This all works well. Now I've started to use naming convention for constraints and my oracle database suddenly complains about a duplicate constraint names.

For debugging and finding a minimal example I used sqlite as the database engine and don't used naming convention (because it seem sqlite just overwrite the first appearance of a constraint name). The code below indeed creates two check constraints with the same content. Why?

**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->
Only one check constraint should be created.

**To Reproduce**
```py
import enum
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Type

from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, create_engine, text, types
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()


class BoolYN(types.TypeDecorator):
    impl = types.Enum

    def __init__(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any):
        super().__init__("Y", "N", *args, **kwargs)

    def process_literal_param(self, value: bool, dialect: Any) -> str:
        """
        Converts bool value passed to literal value on inserting to database.

        aka python --> column
        """
        if value is True:
            return "Y"
        elif value is False:
            return "N"
        else:
            raise TypeError(f"{value} is not of type bool")

    process_bind_param = process_literal_param

    def process_result_value(self, value: str, dialect: Any) -> bool:
        """
        Convert combined enum value to associated single enum type.

        aka column --> python
        """

        if value == "Y":
            return True
        elif value == "N":
            return False
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"{value} cannot be converted to a bool")


class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    active = Column(
        BoolYN(length=1, native_enum=False, create_constraint=True),
        nullable=False,
        server_default=text("'N'"),
    )


def main():
    if Path("custom_type_db.db").exists():
        Path("custom_type_db.db").unlink()

    engine = create_engine("sqlite:///custom_type_db.db", echo="debug")

    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
